The clinical picture is concerning for an *acute, painful, or systemic process* — especially given the age-related inability to localize or verbalize symptoms. While the infant is afebrile, fever is absent in up to 30–40% of serious bacterial infections in young infants, and “ill appearance” (irritability + anorexia) alone warrants full sepsis evaluation.  

The slightly elevated CRP supports low-grade inflammation/infection but is nonspecific. Normal CBC does not rule out UTI, meningitis, or early sepsis — particularly in infants, where leukocytosis may be absent or blunted. All high-yield diagnostic studies are appropriately ordered: urine studies (UTI), CSF analysis (meningitis/encephalitis), abdominal US (surgical abdomen), blood culture (bacteremia), stool studies (infectious gastroenteritis), metabolic labs (lactate, glucose, electrolytes), and CXR (occult pneumonia or viral illness).
